subject: Re: JAX-RTM kickoff — gradient-based retrieval for assimilation
body: Status. Setup milestone: done on schedule — the Ping Yang ice-crystal single-scattering database is integrated and forward simulations validate against the reference radiances (channel-level agreement within calibration tolerance). Retrieval demo: working end-to-end as of last week. Starting from perturbed first guesses, gradient descent through the differentiable solver recovers ice water content and effective radius against real satellite observations; on our 40-scene test set, IWC retrievals land within 12% of the reference analysis on 34 scenes, and the failures are all mixed-phase clouds where the ice-only microphysics assumption breaks. Spatial-alignment optimization helps more than expected — letting the gradient adjust alignment removes most of the parallax artifacts. Risks: (1) mixed-phase handling is a real scope question for the June decision; (2) per-retrieval cost is ~3 GPU-minutes, which sizes the July runs at roughly 900 GPU-hours per full-orbit batch — Jelena has the numbers for the compute ask. — Freya
